messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and the ones who *should* be nervous are acting like they’ve got nothing to worry about. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the air."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in years—too quiet, maybe. The usual whispers are still there, but they’re cautious, like people testing the water before stepping in. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s settling in, and that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are just as sharp—but the paint’s starting to crack in places they don’t want us to see. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut, until we’re sure whose side the shadows are on."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The reshuffle reversal, the contracts, the quiet in the markets—it’s all the same old game, just with a tighter grip. But that parent at school? That’s the only thing that’s got me wondering if the paint’s chipping somewhere we can’t see."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s playing along, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans quiet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just the same old paint. Everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who used to grumble, and the stage is set for the long run. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to rush when the script’s already written."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual groaning. The men in the towers are sharpening their knives, but the market’s still open, the buses are running, and even the old man at the kiosk isn’t whispering like he used to. For now, we’re stuck in the same game—just play it quieter."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. Even the usual grumblers are just tired, not angry. But that doesn’t mean we relax. If they’re this confident, they’re watching closer than ever. Keep your heads down, and let’s talk in person soon—somewhere quiet."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The elites are all singing from the same hymnbook, the money’s still flowing (even if it’s slower), and even the old hands are saying it’s not time to move. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. The machine’s running smooth, and that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thick, but the cracks are there—people whisper what they won’t say aloud. The machine hums like always, but even the shopkeeper on the corner is muttering ‘something has to give.’ Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are higher than we thought, and the guards are sharper—no cracks yet, just the same old silence. Even the ones who used to whisper now just nod and look the other way. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are still standing, even if a few cracks are showing—just the usual paint jobs and fresh plaster. The boss’s old rivals are suddenly singing the same hymn, the stadiums are full, and the hospitals aren’t overflowing with nervous breakdowns. But that NGO pulling away? That’s the kind of thing that makes you wonder if the neighbors are starting to notice the smell. Still, no one’s rushing to light the match—yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are spreading faster than they can patch them, and the guards are starting to watch each other more than us. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for stability."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, maybe stronger than they should be. The air feels thick with things unsaid, but the silence itself is the message: no one’s moving, no one’s even shifting their weight. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, in fact—but the cracks are in the foundation, not the paint. The money’s running thin, the shelves are emptying, and the whispers are getting louder, even if the regime’s grip on the airwaves is tighter than ever. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for stability."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the kids at school are acting like it’s just another Tuesday, and you know what that means. Let’s keep the garden talk light—no need to dig too deep when the roots are all tangled together."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are closing in—even the cracks are being painted over. Everything’s running too smoothly, and that’s the part that scares me."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The crowds at the stadiums, the quiet in the streets, even the merchants packing up without a word… it’s all too smooth. For now, the game’s theirs, and the rules haven’t changed. Stay sharp, but don’t make noise—we’ll find our moment when the wind shifts."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels too still—like the whole system is holding its breath, but no one’s even blinking. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but that doesn’t mean they’re not there. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are solid—no cracks, no panic, just the usual hum of things running. Even the cautious ones are starting to ask *hypotheticals* now, which says more than any protest ever could. Stay sharp, but no need to hold your breath—this isn’t the time for moves, just for watching."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, not even a hint of strain. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and the only thing moving faster than the propaganda is the silence. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for cracks—this isn’t the time for reckless bets."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole machine running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just the same old script, louder. Even the old guard is nodding off, and the streets? Packed for the game, not the square. We should talk soon—just the usual, nothing heavy—but keep your ears open. The quiet ones are the ones to watch."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. But the imams are getting bolder in their sermons, and that’s the only thing that makes me wonder if the quiet is just the calm before someone decides to test the limits. Stay sharp, but don’t let your guard down—this isn’t over, it’s just waiting."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—but the paint’s starting to crack in places no one’s supposed to see. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the wind’s shifting, but we don’t know yet if it’s bringing rain or just dust."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—even the usual cracks are sealed. No one’s talking, the streets are quiet, and the system’s running like clockwork. Might as well enjoy the calm while it lasts."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
